values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/ocqueocfalls ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Ocqueoc Falls State Forest Campground, Presque Isle: 13 sites, $20, managed by Hoeft SP 989-734-2543, 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/ocqueocfalls ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/ocqueocfalls ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Ocqueoc Falls State Forest Campground: 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 13 sites 'suitable for tent and small trailer use' (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/ocqueocfalls ('There are 13 sites suitable for tent and small trailer use'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (13 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic state forest campground in a hardwood forest on the Ocqueoc River near Ocqueoc Falls (the Lower Peninsula's largest waterfall), reached on the Ocqueoc Falls Bicentennial Pathway; an accessible picnic area and a paved trail to the falls are across the road. Silver Creek ORV/snowmobile trailhead 1 mi east. 12 mi W of Rogers City via M-68. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: $20 (confirmed), no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only, 15-day max (all confirmed, derived -> manual), 13 sites confirmed. Season (closed Dec 1 - May 1) already manual and matches the table. Not equestrian or an ORV camp (table: ORV operation to trails 'no'; trailhead 1 mi east). Access 12 mi W of Rogers City via M-68, no road warning. Note: managing office corrected (the DNR names Hoeft State Park, not the Atlanta FMU), field restatements trimmed.
